name: Ho Chi Minh City food guide
summary: Ho Chi Minh City eats from every region, and hủ tiếu is the bowl that belongs here, while phở is best in Hanoi. The southern phở is sweeter and darker, and the table also holds bánh tráng trộn, bún bò Nam Bộ, xôi, and chè beside cơm tấm, bánh mì, and bánh xèo.
body: Hanoi’s cooking is more delicate and lighter on seasoning. This city mixes ingredients and recipes from many regions, and what was born here is still best here.

Two phở bowls sit side by side. Northern-style rooms keep a light, clear, less sweet broth. The southern bowl is sweeter, darker from grilled purple onions and spices, with bean sprouts, raw vegetables, sliced onions, garlic, and soy sauce. Phở bò is on Bùi Viện, beside bánh mì and cơm tấm.
specialtiesLead: Start with cơm tấm, hủ tiếu, bánh mì, bánh xèo, gỏi cuốn, and cà phê sữa đá. Bánh tráng trộn, bún bò Nam Bộ, xôi, and chè sit on the same table.

sections.heading: Regional dishes
paragraphs: These plates are eaten here too. Phở is one of them, and it is still best in Hanoi, which is why hủ tiếu is the bowl to order in this city. Bánh tráng trộn, bún bò Nam Bộ, the Huế bowl as it is eaten here, xôi, and a long list of chè stay on the table, and so does a sweeter southern phở. Phở bò is on Bùi Viện.

spots.name: Oc
spots.note: Ốc is the evening snail plate on Vĩnh Khánh from about 6 p.m.: sweet snails, cockles, and razor clams, stir-fried with butter and garlic, grilled with sea salt and chili, or stewed in coconut milk, and also boiled, steamed, roasted, or sautéed from the shell with a cold beer, with ginger chilli, salted egg, or tamarind sauce. The District 4 spread adds crab, scallops, molluscs, and freshwater snails in butter, garlic, lemongrass, and chili.

spots.name: Bun thit nuong
spots.note: Bún thịt nướng is grilled pork with rice noodles, sold from afternoon sidewalk stalls beside cơm tấm.

spots.name: Banh beo
spots.note: Bánh bèo is small steamed rice cakes, translucent morsels filled with shrimp and pork, often eight to ten in a shared order, with a savory sauce. This is the city’s cake, not the Huế recipe.

spots.name: Banh cuon
spots.note: Bánh cuốn is steamed rice rolls filled with mushrooms, black fungus, and ground pork, made to share.

spots.name: Bo la lot
spots.note: Bò lá lốt is marinated beef in piper lolot leaves, with rice noodles, fresh herbs, and rice paper. You roll them yourself and dip in fish sauce.

spots.name: Bo kho
spots.note: Bò kho is a beef stew of beef chunks and vegetables, with chili and lime, served with a fresh roll.

spots.name: Banh canh cua
spots.note: Bánh canh cua is a seafood soup of crab and shrimp with rice or tapioca noodles in a pork broth, finished with fresh toppings. Stall 1301 at Bến Thành serves it in a hearty broth.

spots.name: Banh da xuc hen
spots.note: Bánh đa xúc hến is tiny fried clams with lemongrass, chili, onion, garlic, and coriander, plus peanuts and a few sesame crackers. It is not bánh đa cua.

spots.name: Pha lau
spots.note: Phá lấu is a Ho Chi Minh City staple, eaten on Hồ Thị Kỷ beside tamarind-seed sweet soup.

spots.name: Tamarind-seed sweet soup
spots.note: Tamarind-seed sweet soup is the dessert cup beside phá lấu on Hồ Thị Kỷ.

spots.name: Bun Thai
spots.note: Bún Thái is the afternoon bowl at alley 76 of Hai Bà Trưng, from 15:00 to 18:00.

spots.name: Bun rieu
spots.note: Bún riêu at Bến Thành is crab meat, pork blood curd, and tofu in a rich broth. Alley 76 of Hai Bà Trưng also serves bún riêu in that afternoon rush.

spots.name: Chicken and rice
spots.note: Chicken and rice is the hearty late lunch or early dinner at alley 76 of Hai Bà Trưng.

spots.name: Grilled skewers
spots.note: The skewers at alley 76 of Hai Bà Trưng come off the barbecue to order, still hot.

spots.name: Bot chien
spots.note: Bột chiên is fried dough with egg and shredded papaya, the plate at alley 76 when you do not want noodles.

spots.name: Mangosteen chicken salad
spots.note: Mangosteen chicken salad is chicken and mangosteen in a salad, in the same company as bánh mì, phở, and cơm tấm.

spots.name: Stingray hotpot
spots.note: Stingray hotpot is a hotpot of stingray, in the same company as mangosteen chicken salad, bánh mì, phở, and cơm tấm.

spots.name: Pho
spots.note: Phở here is two bowls: a light, clear, less sweet northern broth, and a sweeter southern broth darkened with grilled purple onions and spices, with bean sprouts, raw vegetables, sliced onions, garlic, and soy sauce. Phở bò is on Bùi Viện, and the bowl is still best in Hanoi.

spots.name: Banh trang tron
spots.note: Bánh tráng trộn is a snack of rice paper dried in dew and cut small, mixed with shredded green mango, laksa leaves, Tây Ninh shrimp salt, and kumquat juice, then fried onion fat, peanuts, roasted shrimp, quail eggs, and beef jerky. You find it at Turtle Lake, Nguyễn Thượng Hiền in District 3, September 23 Park, the Bến Thành area, and the corner of Nguyễn Thái Học and Trần Hưng Đạo.

spots.name: Bun bo Nam Bo
spots.note: Bún bò Nam Bộ is a brothless plate of small rice vermicelli and thinly sliced stir-fried beef, with a spicy, sour chilli-garlic fish sauce, bean sprouts, cucumber, fried shallots, and roasted peanuts. It is the southern plate, unlike the Huế bowl.

spots.name: Bun bo Hue
spots.note: The bún bò Huế here looks fuller than in Huế: more meat and rolls, beef with pork sausage and fresh vegetables, in a rich spicy broth. A sweet note of sugar softens the strong smell of shrimp paste.

spots.name: Sweet sticky rice
spots.note: Sweet sticky rice is a layer of soft, hot sticky rice with a little grated coconut, then sugar and roasted peanuts. Beans, durian, corn, and sweet gourd are the sweet toppings, sold from morning until late at night.

spots.name: Corn sticky rice
spots.note: Corn sticky rice is sticky corn stewed in coconut water until the seeds are soft and bright white, a bit mushy, sweet but not greasy. Grated coconut, sugar, and peanuts or sesame salt go on when you eat.

spots.name: Cade sticky rice
spots.note: Xôi cadé is soft, chewy sticky rice stuffed into fresh banana leaves and topped with a soft layer of cadé made from coconut milk, eggs, flour, and sugar.

spots.name: Meat sticky rice
spots.note: Meat sticky rice comes with xá xíu (roasted pork), dried shrimp, sausage, meat floss, pork rolls, and quail eggs, plus fatty onions or fried shallots and a rich sauce.

spots.name: Chicken sticky rice
spots.note: Chicken sticky rice is marinated chicken thighs on sticky rice with onion fat, pickled mustard greens, and a cooked sauce. Crispy fried chicken skin, eggs, shredded chicken, shumai, and boiled gizzard liver can come alongside.

spots.name: Lotus-seed sweet soup
spots.note: Lotus-seed sweet soup is a chè of lotus seed, sold along streets in Districts 1, 5, and 10.

spots.name: Green-bean sweet soup
spots.note: Green-bean sweet soup is a chè of green beans, separate from the bean cup and the white-bean cup on the Su Van Hanh tray.

spots.name: Red-bean sweet soup
spots.note: Red-bean sweet soup is a chè of red beans, separate from the bean cup on the Su Van Hanh tray, sold along streets in Districts 1, 5, and 10.

spots.name: Peanut sweet soup
spots.note: Peanut sweet soup is a chè of peanuts, sold along streets in Districts 1, 5, and 10.

spots.name: Black-sesame sweet soup
spots.note: Black-sesame sweet soup is a chè of black sesame, sold along streets in Districts 1, 5, and 10.

spots.name: Longan sweet soup
spots.note: Longan sweet soup is a chè of longan, sold along streets in Districts 1, 5, and 10.

spots.name: Ginkgo sweet soup
spots.note: Ginkgo sweet soup is a chè of ginkgo, sold along streets in Districts 1, 5, and 10.

spots.name: Water-chestnut sweet soup
spots.note: Water-chestnut sweet soup is a chè of water chestnut, sold along streets in Districts 1, 5, and 10.

spots.name: Ginseng-tonic sweet soup
spots.note: Ginseng-tonic sweet soup is a chè of ginseng tonic, sold along streets in Districts 1, 5, and 10.

spots.name: Braised chicken egg
spots.note: Braised chicken egg is a sweet-soup cup like flan. The flan on the Su Van Hanh tray is a separate plate.

spots.name: Chicken egg soaked in black tea
spots.note: Chicken egg soaked in black tea is a sweet-soup cup, sold along streets in Districts 1, 5, and 10.

spots.name: Steamed-papaya sweet soup
spots.note: Steamed-papaya sweet soup is a chè of steamed papaya, sold along streets in Districts 1, 5, and 10.

spots.name: Ba Ba sweet soup
spots.note: Ba Ba is one cup on the 16-cup tray at the sweet-soup shop on Su Van Hanh.

spots.name: Regular bean sweet soup
spots.note: The regular bean sweet soup on the Su Van Hanh tray is made from beans, listed apart from the white-bean cup and from the city’s green-bean and red-bean bowls.

spots.name: Banana sweet soup
spots.note: Banana sweet soup is a cup of banana on the 16-cup tray at the sweet-soup shop on Su Van Hanh.

spots.name: Corn sweet soup
spots.note: Corn sweet soup is a chè of corn on the Su Van Hanh tray, not the corn sticky rice.

spots.name: White-bean sweet soup
spots.note: White-bean sweet soup is the white-bean cup on the Su Van Hanh tray, beside the regular bean sweet soup.

spots.name: Taro sweet soup
spots.note: Taro sweet soup is a cup of taro on the Su Van Hanh tray.

spots.name: Dumplings sweet soup
spots.note: Dumplings sweet soup is a cup of dumplings on the Su Van Hanh tray.

spots.name: Thai sweet soup
spots.note: Thai sweet soup tastes of durian, with a sweet and fatty milk taste.

spots.name: Flan
spots.note: The Su Van Hanh tray comes with a plate of flan, a jar of coconut jelly, and a plate of sticky rice. Braised chicken egg is a separate cup, also like flan.

sections.heading: International dining
paragraphs: The stalls on Bùi Viện serve Vietnamese street food and also Indian, Italian, Chinese, and Thai food. Those four kitchens belong to the street. Quince and Baozi are in Fine dining.

spots.name: Indian kitchens on Bui Vien
spots.note: Indian food is among the stalls and rooms on Bùi Viện. The street became the city’s second official walking street in 2017. Eating starts around dinner and continues all night.

spots.name: Italian kitchens on Bui Vien
spots.note: Italian food is on Bùi Viện, from dinner through the night.

spots.name: Chinese kitchens on Bui Vien
spots.note: Chinese food is on Bùi Viện, from dinner through the night. This is not the Chinatown street in District 5.

spots.name: Thai kitchens on Bui Vien
spots.note: Thai food is on Bùi Viện, from dinner through the night.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: These are the streets and the doors for everyday eating. A door is where a plate is served. It is not a rank.

spots.name: Ben Thanh food end
spots.address: 32-30 Phan Bội Châu, Ben Thanh, District 1
spots.note: The end of the hall is a maze of stalls cooking bánh xèo and assembling bánh mì. The market faces Quách Thị Trang.

spots.name: Vinh Khanh
spots.note: After dark, snails and seafood. The street comes to life around 6 p.m. on weekdays and weekends, and people grill meat and seafood on coal at the table.

spots.name: Nhieu Loc bank
spots.note: Restaurants along this canal, a branch of the Saigon River, serve the same snail-and-seafood evening.

spots.name: Co Giang
spots.note: A Vietnamese street-food stretch at the edge of a block of bars, with barbecue, fryers, and steam under fluorescent lights.

spots.name: Tran Khac Chan
spots.note: A neon strip of eating options, cars and motorbikes mixed with people on foot.

spots.name: Phan Van Han
spots.note: A neighborhood lane at the edge of District 1, for students and locals, with sidewalk tables and bare bulbs.

spots.name: Nguyen Thuong Hien
spots.note: Sidewalk dining for clams, sea snails, crab claws, oysters, fruit juice, and beer, with diners singing along to guitar players. This is not the cơm tấm street.

spots.name: Ho Thi Ky
spots.note: A few hundred meters of food and drink stalls beside the flower wholesale market. Flower trucks come from Đà Lạt and nearby provinces. On the stalls: noodle soups, snails, fruit, cakes, phá lấu, and tamarind-seed sweet soup. Students and workers come after class.

spots.name: Alley 76 Hai Ba Trung
spots.note: Smaller than Hồ Thị Kỷ. The peak is 15:00–18:00: bún Thái, bún riêu, chicken and rice, grilled skewers, and bột chiên with egg and shredded papaya.

spots.name: Bui Vien
spots.address: About 850 m, crossing Đề Thám, Phạm Ngũ Lão, and Đỗ Quang Đẩu
spots.note: Vietnamese stalls, barbecue with beer, bánh mì, phở bò, and seafood. The street never sleeps: dinner, then all night. The Indian, Italian, Chinese, and Thai kitchens are in International dining.

spots.name: A Chinatown food street
spots.note: Food stalls, cafes, and bars line a Chinatown street in District 5.

spots.name: Van Kiep
spots.address: The border of Phú Nhuận and Bình Thạnh
spots.note: Neon signs and a run of Vietnamese dishes draw a young crowd. People come for a rare dish.

spots.name: Com tam Ba Ghien
spots.note: The nearest cơm tấm room, at 84 Đặng Văn Ngữ. The plate is broken rice with grilled pork and sweet fish sauce.

spots.name: Oc Vu
spots.note: A snail door on Vĩnh Khánh for the evening baskets.

spots.name: Oc Oanh
spots.note: Crab, scallops, molluscs, and freshwater snails in butter, garlic, lemongrass, and chili.

spots.name: Hu tieu Ba Hoang
spots.note: The hủ tiếu room at 56 Võ Văn Tần. The broth is delicate, slightly sweet, and clear.

spots.name: Banh mi Huynh Hoa
spots.note: A bánh mì bakery at 26 Lê Thị Riêng, more than half a century old.

spots.name: Banh mi Hoa Ma
spots.note: Bánh mì Hoa Mã on Bùi Viện, a bakery more than half a century old.

spots.name: Goi cuon Minh
spots.note: Fresh rolls and iced tea after a walk, at 84/33 Bùi Viện.

spots.name: Cuc Gach Quan
spots.note: A family-style restaurant in an old house.

spots.name: Quan Bui
spots.note: A room for a Vietnamese dinner.

spots.name: Ben Thanh night market
spots.address: Phan Chu Trinh and Phan Bội Châu, beside Ben Thanh
spots.note: The night market starts at 7:00 PM, with over 100 stalls along those streets. The food is seafood and grilled dishes.

spots.name: Bay Ho Bakery
spots.note: A bánh mì bakery that has lasted more than half a century. Fillings on the city loaf include shumai, pork skin, fish cake, roasted pork, grilled beef, and shredded chicken.

spots.name: Tang banh mi
spots.note: A bánh mì bakery that has lasted more than half a century.

spots.name: Cu Ly banh mi
spots.note: A bánh mì bakery that has lasted more than half a century.

spots.name: Sau Le banh mi
spots.note: A bánh mì bakery that has lasted more than half a century.

spots.name: Su Van Hanh sweet soup
spots.note: Sweet soup with southern flavours. The tray is 16 cups: Ba Ba, a bean sweet soup, banana, corn, white bean, taro, and dumplings, with a jar of coconut jelly, a plate of sticky rice, and a plate of flan.

spots.name: A Thai sweet soup street
spots.note: A street of Thai sweet soup. The bowl smells of durian and tastes of sweet, fatty milk.

spots.name: Che Be
spots.address: Stall 1154–1130, West Side, Gate 7, Ben Thanh, Phan Chu Trinh, District 1
spots.note: The renowned chè stall in Bến Thành, more than 40 years of southern-style chè, with the cups in glass cases.

sections.heading: Fine dining
paragraphs: Quince, Baozi, and Anan are the fine-dining rooms. The city also has Michelin-recognised restaurants beyond these three.

spots.name: Quince Saigon
spots.note: Mediterranean, expanded from Bangkok. The plates use local produce and imported ingredients, grilled on a wood-burning stove, with a wine list. Solo diners can sit at the bar, and an upstairs room seats larger parties.

spots.name: Baozi
spots.note: Taiwanese, in a funky, hip, modern room. A Vietnamese-British founder brought a bao concept from London. Taiwanese bao are open, unlike the closed Vietnamese bánh bao. The founder recommends scotch eggs, ramen, teriyaki ribs, pork belly rice, and the carrot cake.

spots.name: Anan Saigon
spots.note: Peter Cuong Franklin cooks “Cuisine Moi,” French technique on Vietnamese street food, in the wet market, with a rooftop dining bar. It is the room for a phở with a new perspective, modern and elevated.

sections.heading: Themed dining
paragraphs: Rooms set by the room itself: a rooftop, a sky bar, a brewery, a hotel bar, and the cafe buildings on Đồng Khởi and Nguyễn Huệ.

spots.name: Vo Roof Garden
spots.note: Modern Vietnamese dishes on a rooftop.

spots.name: L'Usine
spots.note: A cold coffee on the Đồng Khởi shopping walk.

spots.name: 42 Nguyen Hue
spots.note: A former apartment block of cafes and shops. It is a building, not one restaurant.

spots.name: Do Phu Cafe
spots.note: Sidewalk coffee at Turtle Lake, and traditional cloth-filter coffee.

spots.name: Turtle Lake sidewalk coffee
spots.note: Sidewalk coffee at Turtle Lake.

spots.name: Saigon Saigon Bar
spots.note: The bar at the Caravelle.

spots.name: Pasteur Street Brewing Company
spots.note: A brewery.

spots.name: Glow Sky Bar
spots.note: A sky bar.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Cơm tấm is the breakfast, and people also eat it at any meal: breakfast, lunch, dinner, or supper. Sticky rice is sold in the morning, at noon, in the afternoon, in the evening, and late at night. Bánh mì starts a morning and is sold at any hour. Cà phê sữa đá is the Saturday morning cup in the park outside the palace, before you go in.

spots.name: Cafes in the palace park
spots.note: Cà phê sữa đá on a Saturday morning, at the cafes in the park outside the Reunification Palace, before you go in. The coffee is not inside the palace ticket.

spots.name: Tan Dinh Market
spots.note: Sunday morning produce, vegetables, and street-food snacks on Hai Bà Trưng in District 3. It is not Nhà thờ Tân Định.

seoTitle: Ho Chi Minh City food — cơm tấm, hủ tiếu, bánh tráng trộn
seoDescription: Cơm tấm, hủ tiếu, bánh mì, bánh tráng trộn, bún bò Nam Bộ, xôi, and chè in Ho Chi Minh City. Phở is best in Hanoi, and the southern bowl here is sweeter.
